relevance_note: Single-patient follow-up case report of a woman with a GFAP variant and Alexander disease: "The patient is a 44-year-old woman carrying the p.R70Q and p.D157N GFAP mutations with adult-onset AxD".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON and checked spans. One in-scope person, the single unnamed patient of the case report (label 'patient'); the paper states she was reported before (Sechi et al. 2010a), so cites_prior_report is true. Two GFAP variants are printed only as protein strings (p.R70Q and p.D157N); the paper gives no zygosity, phase (cis/trans), inheritance, variant class or classification beyond calling them 'mutations', so those fields are 'not reported'. Age 44 is taken as age at report ('The patient is a 44-year-old woman'). Feature onsets 'After about 16 months', 'After 3.5 years' and 'After 7 months of therapy' are times relative to the study or therapy start, not ages, so onset_iso8601 is null for them. Eye movement recording was normal and there was no oscillopsia at the beginning of the study, but both later became abnormal; these are time-dependent, not contradictions, so no excluded rows were emitted for them and the checklist item is observed. 'Palatal myoclonus' was mapped to the checklist item 'palatal tremor' (the paper never uses the word tremor). High signal in the pyramidal tracts of the medulla is imaging, not a clinical pyramidal sign, so 'spasticity or pyramidal signs' is not reported. MMSE score of 30 is stated but the paper does not call it normal, so 'cognitive decline' is not reported. EEG without epileptiform activity does not exclude the broader item 'seizures' (left not reported); the myoclonic jerks in the upper limbs (an adverse event during ceftriaxone) were not called seizures by the authors. Normal periodic laboratory controls, ECG and EEG were recorded as excluded abnormalities under D-27. Periventricular high signal was not described as a rim, so 'periventricular rim' is not reported. No contradictions found.

treatment_summary.value: Intravenous ceftriaxone 2 g daily, for 3 weeks monthly during the initial 4 months, then for 15 days monthly, for 4 years (via a chronic subcutaneously implanted port); a probiotic preparation (FlorVis-gg, Lactobacillus rhamnosus) by mouth once daily among the ceftriaxone cycles; miconazole for a mycotic vaginal infection; the patient refused any therapy for myoclonic jerks.
span: for the following 4 years, after intravenous ceftriaxone 2 g daily, for 3 weeks monthly during the initial 4 months, then for 15 days monthly
Among the ceftriaxone cycles, a probiotic preparation was administered by mouth once daily: FlorVis-gg, containing 6 milliards of Lactobacillus rhamnosus.
Intravenous ceftriaxone was administered by a chronic subcutaneously implanted port on the chest.
After 7 months of therapy, the patient had a mycotic vaginal infection treated with miconazole.
The patient refused any therapy for myoclonic jerks.
